findings.title: A withdrawal on the other network, which would tie a stake-key certificate to it: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: The wallet is on preprod. A site calls signTx(tx, true). The tx has one input the wallet can't find (the site's own UTxO on mainnet), no outputs, no network id, a StakeDelegation of the account's stake credential to pool P, and a withdrawal of 0 from the account's mainnet reward address. With the check, inspect refuses: 'This transaction withdraws from mainnet, and the wallet is on preprod.' Without it, the withdrawal counts as the account's own (the stake key signs) and as the transaction's network tie (`tied` reads body.withdrawals.is_some(), trusting this check). So the stake key signs: signs ['stake'], net 0, complete false. The site adds its own witness and submits on mainnet, and the user's mainnet stake is delegated to P. A vote delegation or an UnReg works the same. This is chunk 29's hole (one stake key on both networks) reopened through a withdrawal. Every test that reaches cip30 passes without the check.
findings.since: fe8b7748 (chunk 15's connector, in 1.0.0; first tagged web-wallet/1.6.0). chunk 29's `tied` (b05d8169) leans on it.

Run alone, everything passed: cip30_test 73/73, session_test 14/14, read_value_test 2/2, decode_test 37/37, lib 7/7.

- With M14: sign_tx(partial_sign true) is Ok and prints `signed by ["stake"], net 0 lovelace, certificates 1, complete false`.

Why the existing test misses it: cip30_test's the_stake_key_never_signs_what_could_be_the_other_networks (:1253-1262) ties its bodies with a withdrawal from stake_account_bytes(), which is stake_address(true), preprod's. It never uses the other network's reward address.

findings.title: A launch's unreadable datum beside a script at the holder making the whole pool unreadable: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: A pool-launcher's launch transaction (one_shot_mint checks only the reference output) puts a script output at the holder. It carries the pool's mix_logic as a reference script and an inline datum nested past core's 128 levels (chunk 34's 314-wasm#0 shape, about 37 ₳ to make). Discovery passes every script row of the launch tx in PoolRef.scripts (lovejoin-pools.ts:585), so the row reaches protocol_of. With the skip, the row is no reference: its script is carried inline and the pool verifies. Without it, core's resolve_reference refuses the row ('holds a datum the wallet can't read'), and the `?` fails protocol_of on every call for that pool. The pool is then never verified or shown, and no deposit, mix or withdraw in it builds, so boxes the wallet holds there can't come back through it. The suite passes without the skip.

findings.title: Overflowing ADA and token sums wrapping instead of being refused: no test fails without the checks
findings.scenario: A stranger mints a junk token T, 2^63−1 each time, into three outputs at the account's 0/0 (about 4 ₳, most of it the user's). A site's signTx then spends those three own UTxOs and sends all of T to the site in outputs that conserve value. spent's T is 3·(2^63−1), past a u64. With the checks, inspect refuses: 'a token amount overflows'. Without them, the shipped module wraps: seedelf-wasm has no overflow checks in wasm-release (Cargo.toml's comment). spent's T becomes 2^63−3, so the window's net tokens understate what leaves by about 1.8×10^19 of T. The same goes for duplicate multiasset entries in one output, which Pallas keeps and of_value sums, and for ADA in Amount::add and add_staking. The amounts involved are junk, but the figures shown are false, and no test feeds an overflow.
findings.since: fe8b7748 for add_token and add (chunk 15, in 1.0.0); 82e81fe4 for add_staking. First tagged web-wallet/1.6.0.

findings.title: Collateral at risk counted with the site's collateral as if it were the account's: no test fails without the own-only sum
findings.scenario: A site's transaction puts up two collateral UTxOs: the account's 5 ₳, and the site's own 10 ₳ (found through Koios). Its collateral return pays 12 ₳ to the account's own address. findings.title: A stranger's 5 ₳ UTxO with a datum, a token, a reference script or another value taken as the session's collateral for its mix: no test fails without fits_collateral's checks

findings.title: Chain change sent to a stranger's row's address (the session's key under the stranger's stake key): no test fails without the own-row preference

findings.title: A token total past u64 wrapping the count of token boxes: no test fails without the u128 sum
findings.scenario: A session's own UTxOs (its funding, or a fill's) hold the token pool's token in three outputs of 2^63−1 each (one mint holds at most 2^63−1). guards.stops: A site's transaction over 64 KiB is refused before any decode (M01: cap removed)

A body network_id of the other network is refused (M03)
An input or collateral row at a Shelley address on the other network is refused (M04)
owner(): a found input or collateral at the stake key's hash (M05a) or the DRep key's (M05b) is the account's
With the account's collateral in, a collateral return to someone else is refused (M06)
A collateral return on the other network is refused (M07)
at_risk = the account's collateral less what returns to it. M08a drops the subtraction; M08b counts the site's found collateral as the account's (the mixed case)
A transaction marked to fail with the account's collateral is refused (M09)
An output on the other network (Byron by its magic) is refused (M10)
own_address is the account's payment key AND its stake key. M11a: any stake key. M11b: any staking part. M11c: the ownPaymentKey flag dropped
A pool registration naming the account's stake key an owner is refused (M12)
An old deregistration without a known deposit is refused (M13a); with one, its refund is counted (M13b)
A withdrawal from a reward address on the other network is refused (M14); it is also what lets a withdrawal tie a transaction to this network
A proposal whose deposit returns on the other network is refused (M15)
A payment key's signature (M16a) or the DRep key's (M16b) over an input the wallet can't find is refused
No signature over a transaction that nothing ties to the wallet's network (M17)

notes:
How the runs worked:
- Every Rust mutant was compiled once into the copy, each behind its own switch `crate::r51("<id>")` that reads R51_MUT and is off by default.
- A control run with every switch off matched the clean baseline exactly: 14 binaries, same counts.
- Each mutant then ran alone (R51_MUT=<id>); the evidence quotes each change as the plain code edit.
- The checked-sum mutants use wrapping_add, which is what the shipped module does: seedelf-wasm has no overflow checks in wasm-release. Tests run in the dev profile.
- TypeScript mutants were applied to the copy's lovejoin.ts from a pristine backup, run through Vitest, and restored after each run.
- 76 mutants in all: 35 in cip30.rs and decode.rs, 29 in wasm lovejoin.rs, 3 in seedelf-core, 9 in lovejoin.ts.

Lane W3's lovejoin.ts:4232 entry says takesNewBoxes is the only refusal of new boxes into a retired pool. It isn't:
- usableNow (4199) refuses a retired pool too, which masks takesNewBoxes' own check wherever pool.ref is set.
- publicBuild (4857) and publicAgainBuild (5015) check isRetired themselves.
- chain() (3691) sends a retired pool's Mix again to takesNewBoxes.
All of these, adaPoolOf and tailChain are pinned by the retire tests.

raw_vkeys' Vec::new (cip30.rs:2041) is an equivalent mutant, so no test can or needs to catch it. Both of raw_vkeys' callers pass bytes that raw_item has already skipped whole, so a count can't exceed its bytes. The guard that matters, raw_map's, is caught.

Masked or doubled guards:
- protocols_of's two checks: each is masked by the other in the only test (t1f#12).
- mixes_collateral (lovejoin.rs:984): caught only by its words; core refuses the same chain.
- our_box (2665): caught because core's withdraw_with checks ownership again.
- verify_pool's datum script-hash check: pinned only by seedelf-core's test. The wasm tests the lane named don't fail without it.
- fits_collateral's token condition: Coin::from_row refuses a token row anyway, so without it the tail is dropped (`.ok()`) rather than built wrong.

For the owner: the stack overflow behind 314-wasm#0 (a hostile pool's deep datum at the holder) is now stopped in core: eval::resolve_reference checks unreadable_datum before decoding. The skip at lovejoin.rs:195 is what keeps such a pool readable instead of refused; t1f#2 pins it. Discovery takes a pool's script rows only from its launch transaction (lovejoin-pools.ts:509 and :585), so only the pool-launcher can plant one.

For the Lovejoin/privacy lanes, a doubt I traced but didn't run: direct_tail (lovejoin.rs:434-437) takes the FIRST session UTxO that fits_collateral accepts. It doesn't use the session's named collateral, as the chain's path does. A stranger's plain 5 ₳ ADA-only UTxO, listed before the session's own collateral, would be boxed in its place. The session's collateral would then pay as a coin and its ADA come back through the change, unmixed. That's a privacy downgrade a stranger buys for 5 ₳ (which becomes the user's). It's worth checking against independent review L20 and the worker's collateralFits.
